previous_admission_summary.summary_paragraph: Mr. Johnson, a patient with hepatitis C-related cirrhosis and hepatocellular carcinoma, was admitted for observation following a transarterial chemoembolization (TACE) procedure targeting a residual liver tumor in segment II. He had previously undergone radiofrequency ablation, which was complicated by a hemothorax. This admission was marked by post-procedural nausea and a low-grade fever, for which he received IV anti-emetics and a course of ciprofloxacin. Blood and urine cultures showed no growth. He developed a new headache, prompting a head CT that ruled out intracranial hemorrhage. His thrombocytopenia remained stable without bleeding. He improved clinically, with resolution of symptoms, and was discharged home on oral medications with instructions to complete antibiotics, manage nausea and pain as needed, and follow up as an outpatient.
problems: Cirrhosis of liver without mention of alcohol
Chronic hepatitis C without mention of hepatic coma

radiology_notes.text:
REASON FOR THE EXAMINATION:  ___ man with HCC, after TACE, for
followup.

COMPARISON:  CT of the abdomen without contrast from ___ and CTA of the
abdomen from ___.

TECHNIQUE:  Multidetector CT with IV contrast administration.  Sagittal and
coronal reformations were made.

FINDINGS:  The lungs bases are within normal limits.  The base of the heart is
mildly enlarged.

ABDOMEN:  A known cirrhotic liver.  Stable appearance of an RF ablated lesion
in segment VI with no signs of enhancement within or in proximity to the
lesion.  Two foci of Ethiodol contrast is seen in segment II and III the
largest measures 15x12 mm and is located in the previous arterial enhancing
lesion.  No new arterially enhancing lesions are detected within the liver. 
The portal vein is of normal caliber and patent.  The hepatic veins are of
normal caliber and patent.  Recanalized paraumbilical vein is observed. 
Esophageal, gastric, and splenorenal varices are noted. The spleen is enlarged
measuring 15 cm.  The pancreas is within normal limits.  The adrenals are
unremarkable.  Both kidneys enhance and secretes adequately.  A known
gallbladder stone is seen.  No intra- or extra-biliary duct dilatation.   . 
The large and small bowel are with no gross pathology except for nonspecific
thickening of the cecum and proximal part of the ascending colon.  Mild
hyperemia of mesenteric vessels are observed, most probably secondary to
portal hypertension.  Few non-suspicious lymph nodes are seen in the RLQ
(series 6, image 45, series 6, image 49).  No retroperitoneal lymph nodes are
observed.

The aorta and its large vessels are patent.  Of note, replaced right hepatic
artery is seen originating from the SMA.

BONY WINDOW:  Degenerative changes are seen along the spine.

IMPRESSION:  
1. Two foci of Ethiodol contrast is seen in segment II and III the largest
measures 15x12 mm and is located in the previous arterial enhancing lesion.
2. No new enhancing lesions are seen within the liver.  
3. Stable appearance of RF ablated lesion in segment VI.
4. Thickening of the cecum and proximal part of the ascending colon most
probably secondary to portal hypertension still the examination is limited due
to lack of oral contrast media
